title: Proper schematic image of a proper algebraic-space family
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:X\to T$, $q:Y\to T$, and $h:X\to Y$ satisfy $qh=p$. Assume that $p$ is proper and $q$ is separated and locally of finite type, with these properties as in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. There exist an algebraic space $Z$ over $T$, a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, and a morphism $u:X\to Z$ over $T$ with $h=iu$, such that $Z\to T$ is proper and the point map $|u|:|X|\to|Z|$ is surjective. Moreover $Z$ is the smallest closed subspace of $Y$ through which $h$ factors (its scheme-theoretic image): for every closed subspace $W\hookrightarrow Y$ through which $h$ factors, the inclusion $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ factors through $W$. Here closed immersion means representable with every scheme base change a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and point spaces and their maps are those of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. No Noetherian, reducedness, flatness, or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AGD, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-is-proper; the smallest-closed-subspace characterization is Tag 082X, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image, used in that lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-cancellation] to $h:X\to Y$ and $q:Y\to T$: their composite is the proper map $p$, and $q$ is separated. Thus $h$ is proper, in particular of finite type. We may use algebraic-stack statements for these spaces: regard their sheaves as discrete fibred groupoids as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Descent of objects is precisely sheaf descent, and scheme tests of the diagonal are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; a representable surjective etale scheme atlas is a smooth atlas by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Thus these are algebraic (indeed Deligne--Mumford) stacks, and $h$ is representable by algebraic spaces. The stack and space finite-type notions agree by [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], whose ordinary algebraic-space quasi-compactness tests every quasi-compact algebraic space; hence $X\times_YC$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C\to Y$. For a scheme $T\to Y$ and a quasi-compact space $C\to T$ one has $X_T\times_TC=X\times_YC$, so every scheme base change $h_T$ is quasi-compact as a morphism of algebraic spaces in the sense of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. By (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-sfb-representable-stack-quasicompact-tests], $h$ is quasi-compact as a stack morphism in the convention of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]: $X\times_Y\mathcal V$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal V\to Y$. The point topologies agree by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology].

source.place: Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), giving the quasi-compactness of h used in the proof of Tag 0AGD; discrete-stack convention for applying the already existing schematic-image theorem

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-schematic-image-qc] to the quasi-compact morphism $h$ of step 1. It supplies a closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, given on etale scheme charts by the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to h_*\mathcal O_X)$, a factorization $h=iu$, minimal among all closed subspaces through which $h$ factors, and identifies $|Z|$ with the closure of $|h|(|X|)$. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], closed subspaces given by quasi-coherent ideals are exactly the subfunctors whose inclusion is representable by closed immersions of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], by an inclusion-reversing bijection; so $i$ is a closed immersion in the sense of the statement, and the minimality just quoted is minimality among all such closed immersions $W\hookrightarrow Y$ through which $h$ factors, with their full ideal structure. Put $r=q i:Z\to T$; then $ru=p$, so the factorization is over $T$. This is a scheme-theoretic factorization, not a factorization inferred merely from point-set containment.

Step 1 makes $h$ universally closed by the definition in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], hence $|h|(|X|)$ is closed in $|Y|$. Its closure is therefore itself. The equality from step 2 gives $|i|(|Z|)=|h|(|X|)$. A closed immersion has injective point map by [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus], in the compatible topology of step 1. For $z\in|Z|$, choose $x\in|X|$ with $|h|(x)=|i|(z)$; then $|i|(|u|(x))=|i|(z)$ implies $|u|(x)=z$. Thus $|u|$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0AGD (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-is-proper), closed plus dense implies surjective, with Tag 04NX (lemma-universally-closed-permanence) for closedness of the image

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], hence separated and locally of finite type by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Its composite $r=q i$ is separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], since $q$ is separated. Both $i$ and $q$ are locally of finite type, so $r$ is locally of finite type by the composition clause of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], whose statement identifies the stack and algebraic-space notions. No finite-presentation property of $i$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0AGD, hypotheses for Tag 08AJ (lemma-image-proper-is-proper); finite type requires quasi-compactness, established separately in step 6

proof.text: For every algebraic space $T^{\prime}\to T$, use the sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] to put $X^{\prime}=X\times_TT^{\prime}$ and $Z^{\prime}=Z\times_TT^{\prime}$. The map $u^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to Z^{\prime}$ is the base change of $u$, and is point-surjective by the fibre-product point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The map $p^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. If $C\subseteq|Z^{\prime}|$ is closed, continuity of $|u^{\prime}|$ makes $D=|u^{\prime}|^{-1}(C)$ closed. Surjectivity gives $|r^{\prime}|(C)=|p^{\prime}|(D)$, which is closed because $p^{\prime}$ is universally closed. Thus $r$ is universally closed by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

source.place: Tag 08AJ (lemma-image-proper-is-proper), proof: surjectivity after base change and image of an inverse-image closed subset

proof.text: For every quasi-compact algebraic space $A\to T$, the all-test quasi-compactness clause in [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus] gives quasi-compact $X_A$, since $p$ is of finite type. Choose a surjective etale atlas $W\to X_A$ with $W$ a quasi-compact scheme, as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Its point map is surjective and continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Hence the composite $|W|\to|Z_A|$ is surjective and continuous by step 5. An open cover of $|Z_A|$ pulls back to an open cover of $W$; a finite subcover exists by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and surjectivity makes the corresponding opens cover $|Z_A|$. Thus $|Z_A|$ is quasi-compact, and [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] supplies an affine etale atlas, so $Z_A$ is quasi-compact as an algebraic space. Since this holds for every $A$, $r$ is quasi-compact. Together with steps 4 and 5, [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] makes $r$ proper. Steps 2 and 3 give minimality, factorization and surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 08AJ (lemma-image-proper-is-proper), finite-type qualification, and Tag 0AGD (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-is-proper), conclusion

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q41-745b7bd4b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Not superseded: the live node is still unsplit and there is no repair note. The delivery is a six-step split with no new nodes and no statement change. Read against Stacks 0AGD (spaces-morphisms l.8015) and 08AJ (l.7994). The hypotheses match, with B specialized to the scheme T, and minimality follows 082X. Two citation faults, both repaired. (1) C4, step 1: the step took 'h is quasi-compact in the stack convention' from lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus. That node's stack quasi-compactness is the affine point-space test, but lem-sfb-stack-schematic-image-qc needs the def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism convention, which tests against every quasi-compact stack. Repair: the ordinary all-test quasi-compactness from finite-type-calculus, plus X_T×_T C=X×_Y C, gives (i) of lem-sfb-representable-stack-quasicompact-tests (same unit); its (i)⇒(ii) is exactly the needed convention. The step's source place is changed from 04NX to 073B. (2) C1/C4, step 2: the schematic-image node gives a closed subspace defined by a quasi-coherent ideal on étale charts. The item and the closed-immersion calculus of step 3 need a representable closed immersion, and the item's minimality ranges over those. Repair: cite lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence, an inclusion-reversing bijection with a factorization criterion, so both the closed-immersion property and minimality carry over. Steps 3–6 are correct. Step 3: closed image plus injective |i| gives a surjective |u|. Step 4: separated composition clause and the lft composition clause for DM stacks. Step 5: the closed-set argument of 08AJ after an arbitrary base change, with surjectivity from the point-image formula. Step 6: |Z_A| is quasi-compact as a continuous image, which for affine A is the def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli convention. Edge cases checked: X empty, h a closed immersion, a non-quasi-compact Y, and non-Noetherian T. Tool uses accepted: lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers and lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus, both generic foundations; the copied 'why' of the second is rewritten. All 13 batch-5 flags reach sec-trace-formula only through the definition def-trf-algebraic-space or the generic fibre-product lemma, so none is a trace-formula or Poincaré-duality step.
